# Independent audit of parity consensus and its simplex-fiber obstruction

Audited independently by the depth/Helly route:

    candidate 233dacf87d7f01e6
    supporting computation verify_parity_consensus_simplex_obstruction.py

Result: PASS. Both the full-sequence convergence theorem and the exact
two-atom selector obstruction are proved with the stated scope. The
Fraction verifier passes. No mathematical correction was needed.

## 1. Operation, weak continuity, and full convergence

The parity class is selected with its original probability p_r. The
class contribution therefore has coefficient 1/p_r against the two
unnormalized restricted source measures, giving total class mass p_r.
Both endpoint marginals are the original measure. This checks the
ordinary full ambient mean preservation and the factor one half in the
within-class covariance-trace loss. The squared norm here is of the
FULL ambient point, including its integer coordinates.

Every midpoint belongs to the actual compact mixed set by convexity and
parity. The finitely many parity classes are relatively clopen in this
set, so restriction to a class is weakly continuous. For a class of
positive limiting mass the product-integral formula is continuous.
For a vanishing class its absolute test contribution is bounded by
p_r times the test supremum, proving continuity at p_r=0 as well.

Jensen applies to every continuous function convex on C; this includes
the polynomial convexifications used next. The Hessian of each ambient
polynomial is bounded below on compact C, so adding a sufficiently large
multiple of the FULL squared norm makes it convex on C. Convexity on C
is all the midpoint Jensen step needs; no global Hessian bound on the
whole ambient space is required. Both convex integrals converge, and
hence every polynomial integral converges.

The restricted real polynomial algebra contains constants and separates
points of compact S. Stone--Weierstrass gives uniform approximation of
every continuous test. The resulting integral sequence is Cauchy for
every such test. Weak compactness supplies a probability limit, and the
test limits identify it uniquely, proving convergence of the FULL
sequence rather than just a subsequence.

Continuity of Q makes the limit fixed. The exact quadratic loss then
vanishes, forcing each nonempty parity restriction to be one point
mass. Those points lie in S, their parity classes are distinct, and
their positive weights sum to one. This proves the <=2^n support bound
and preserved barycenter without any depth conclusion.

## 2. The actual simplex L and the exact mixed fibers

The face lambda_1=0 is a three-dimensional tetrahedron. Its parallel
section at lambda_1=beta has three-volume (1-beta)^3 times that of the
face. Shrinking that section about its centroid by t multiplies its
three-volume by t^3. Joining it to an apex at lambda_1=0 produces a
four-simplex of relative volume beta(1-beta)^3 t^3, independently of
the tangential location of that apex. The exact comparison
m<beta(1-beta)^3 makes the specified t lie in (0,1).

All five vertices belong to B and are affinely independent. Four have
first coordinate beta and the remaining apex has coordinate zero, so
the simplex centroid has first coordinate 4beta/5. This verifies (4)
as an actual geometric construction rather than only a volume request.

The ordinary homotheties by r and q give endpoint volumes aV and V,
and their exact Minkowski midpoint is L because r+q=2 and L is convex.
The hull with the middle B therefore has exactly the three claimed
integer fibers. All are positive full-dimensional four-simplices, and
the ambient hull is five dimensional.

## 3. Exact limiting masses and positions

With unnormalized masses the parity normalization produces exactly
a'=a^2/(a+c), c'=c^2/(a+c), and b'=b+2ac/(a+c). Total mass is fixed,
the difference c-a stays 1-a_initial, and the smaller endpoint mass
at least halves at each step. Therefore the three masses converge to
0, 1+2a_initial, and 1-a_initial.

There is no incoming mass to an endpoint from any other base pair.
Its conditional continuous mean thus remains its original simplex
centroid. Weak convergence on the finite base support preserves the
endpoint first moment, identifying the positive limiting endpoint atom
as (1,g_D). Full first-moment conservation then identifies the middle
atom exactly as (g_B+2a g_L)/(1+2a). The limit theorem excludes any
additional points within either surviving parity class.

## 4. Both strict cap certificates

At the endpoint atom an ordinary simplex centroid cap has mass Gamma V.
A sufficiently large positive coefficient of z-1 excludes the other two
compact fibers while retaining this endpoint trace exactly. Its mass is
strictly below Gamma(1+a/2)V.

The middle atom's first coordinate is exactly
1/5-(51/625)a/(1+2a), strictly above beta. The displayed tilted cap has
maximum pre-threshold margin beta on BOTH endpoint fibers, including
all their boundaries; it therefore excludes them completely. Its
middle mass is exactly Gamma[1+(51/500)a/(1+2a)]^4 V.

Since a<1/1000, the inner increment is less than 1/1000. The mean-value
bound with factor (51/125)(1001/1000)^3 is consequently valid, and its
strict comparison with one half is rational. This proves the claimed
strict deficit below Gamma(1+a/2)V for the middle atom. The heavier-atom
domination proposal is also violated, since its unnormalized atom mass
1+2a is larger than 1+a/2. Dividing both laws by 2+a preserves all these
comparisons, so probability and unnormalized formulations agree.

The only simplex-depth fact used for the endpoint is the explicit
facet-parallel centroid cap volume; the middle cap is calculated directly.
No mixed OC theorem, extraction principle, or centroid-depth guarantee
enters the counterexample.

## 5. Verification and scope

The exact verifier passes the construction inequalities, homothety
volumes, centroid coordinate, both strict cap comparisons, and recurrence
invariants. The convergence, actual simplex construction, and all-point
identification above were checked independently of that arithmetic.

The result closes this particular consensus-atom selector, even though
the iteration converges and preserves the full mean. It does not refute
OC, an extraction with adjustable convex source shapes, or every possible
martingale decomposition.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
